'''''Romulea columnae''''', the '''sand crocus''', is a herbaceous perennial in the family [[Iridaceae]]. It is a small plant, with thin narrow leaves, and small scape which has small pink, pale purple or violet pointed flowers with darker veining and a gold or yellow throat. It is native to a wide area ranging from western Europe to the Mediterranean.

==Description==
[[File:Romulea columnae scape.jpg|thumb|''Romulea columnae'' scape not stem]]
''Romulea columnae'' grows from a small [[corm]].<ref name="rare">{{cite web |title=Romulea columnae Purple – RarePlants |url=https://www.rareplants.co.uk/product/romulea-columnae-purple/ |website=www.rareplants.co.uk |accessdate=12 June 2020}}</ref><ref name="Seasonal">{{cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Keith |title=Seasonal Wild Flowers - Sand Crocus |url=http://www.seasonalwildflowers.com/sand-crocus.html |website=www.seasonalwildflowers.com |access-date=8 June 2021}}</ref> 
It has one or two [[basal leaves]],<ref name="southwest">{{cite web |title=UK Wildflowers - Iridaceae - Romulea Columnae |url=https://www.uksouthwest.net/wildflowers/iridaceae/romulea-columnae.html |website=www.uksouthwest.net |accessdate=12 June 2020}}</ref> and several (up to 3,<ref name="Seasonal"/>) cauline (stem) leaves,<ref name="rare"/> They are narrow, wiry and curled,<ref name="rare"/><ref name="Seasonal"/><ref name="southwest"/> and they can grow up to {{convert|10|cm|0|abbr=on}} long.<ref name="Seasonal"/><ref name="southwest"/><ref name=Moggridge>[[John Traherne Moggridge]] {{google books|kWpB5wssmHoC|Contributions to the Flora of Mentone and to a Winter Flora of the Riviera, including the coast from Marseilles to Genoa (1874)|page=93}}</ref> Plants from the [[Romulea]] genus are related to members of the [[crocus]] genus and look very similar but have several differences, including that Romulea plants do not have a white grove in the centre of their leaves.<ref name="Biking">{{cite web |title=An unexpected treat: Romulea columnae |url=https://thebikinggardener.com/2016/02/04/an-unexpected-treat-romulea-columnae/ |website=The Biking Gardener |accessdate=15 June 2020 |language=en |date=4 February 2016}}</ref>
Also, crocus flowers are stemless and grow directly from the corm, while Romulea plants hold their flowers on a green [[Scape (botany)|scape]] of various lengths. ''Romulea columnae'' has a short scape,<ref name="rare"/> of up to {{convert|3|-|20|cm|0|abbr=on}} long.<ref name="Seasonal"/><ref name="southwest"/><ref name="Biking"/> In the UK, it is only between {{convert|3|-|4|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall.<ref name="Seasonal"/><ref name="southwest"/>

It blooms early in the year, from February onwards,<ref name="rare"/> or between March and May.<ref name="Seasonal"/><ref name="southwest"/>
It has one to three flowers per corm,<ref name="rare"/><ref name="southwest"/> most common is a solitary flower,<ref name="southwest"/> which is small and only reaching between 10 and 12 mm across.<ref name="Seasonal"/>
The flowers are funnel-shaped,<ref name="rare"/> and have 6 pointed (at the tip) petals,<ref name="Seasonal"/><ref name="southwest"/> which are equally-sized.<ref name="southwest"/> They are pink,<ref name="southwest"/> pale purple,<ref name="Seasonal"/><ref name="southwest"/><ref name=Moggridge/> or violet.<ref name="rare"/> They are greenish-yellow,<ref name="southwest"/> yellow,<ref name="Seasonal"/> or golden-yellow at the centre or throat.<ref name="rare"/> They have purple,<ref name="Seasonal"/><ref name=Moggridge/> or violet veins or a dark midvein and a pair of lighter lateral veins.<ref name="southwest"/> It has a green [[Bract#Spathe|spathe]] which is thin and spindly.<ref name="Seasonal"/>
It has three [[stamens]], topped by yellow,<ref name="southwest"/> or bright yellow anthers,<ref name="Seasonal"/> and the style is shorter than the stamens.<ref name=Moggridge/>

It reproduces mostly by seed.<ref name="Seasonal"/>

==Taxonomy==
[[File:Romulea columnae kz01.jpg|thumb|''Romulea columnae'' in Morocco]]
It is commonly known as ''sand crocus''<ref name="rare"/><ref name="southwest"/> and occasionally as ''dune crocus.''<ref name=Green>Bryn Green {{google books|8dDZAAAAQBAJ|Countryside Conservation: Land Ecology, Planning and Management (1996)|page=234}}</ref> In Malta, it is known as the ''Lesser sand crocus'' due to another endemic ''Romulea'' species.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mifsud |first1=Stephen |title=Romulea columnae (Lesser sand crocus) : MaltaWildPlants.com - the online Flora of the Maltese Islands. |url=http://www.maltawildplants.com/IRID/Romulea_columnae.php |website=www.maltawildplants.com |accessdate=14 June 2020 |language=en-us |date=23 August 2002}}</ref>

The Latin [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''columnae'' refers to column.<ref name=Jarvis>Dr. Peter Jarvis {{google books|5STMDwAAQBAJ|The Pelagic Dictionary of Natural History of the British Isles (2020)|page=686}}</ref>

It was published and described by 2 Italian botanists, [[Francesco Antonio Sebastiani]] and [[Ernesto Mauri]] in 'Fl. Roman. Prodr.' vol.18 in 1818.<ref>{{cite web |title=Romulea columnae Sebast. & Mauri, Fl. Roman. 18. |url=https://www.ipni.org/n/440703-1 |publisher=ipni.org |accessdate=12 June 2020}}</ref><ref name="Grin">{{cite web |title=Taxon: Romulea columnae Sebast. & Mauri |url=https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxonomydetail.aspx?id=32047 |publisher=npgsweb.ars-grin.gov |accessdate=12 June 2020}}</ref><ref name="kew">{{cite web |title=Romulea columnae Sebast. & Mauri, Fl. Roman. Prodr.: 18 (1818). |url=https://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=324534 |publisher=wcsp.science.kew.org |accessdate=12 June 2020}}</ref><!-- also <ref name="POWO"/> -->

''Romulea columnae'' was verified by [[United States Department of Agriculture]] [[Agricultural Research Service]] on 4 April 2003,<ref name=Grin/> and it is an accepted name by the [[Royal Horticultural Society|RHS]].<ref name=rhs>{{cite web|title=''Romulea columnae'', sand crocus |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/100305/Romulea-columnae/Details |publisher=rhs.org.uk| accessdate=12 June 2020}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
[[File:Romulea columnae 1011.jpg|thumb|''Romulea columnae'' on [[El Hierro]], one of the Canary Islands]]
''Romulea columnae'' is [[native plant|native]] to various [[temperateness|temperate]] areas of western [[Asia]],<ref name=rhs/> Africa and Europe.<ref name=Grin/><ref name="kew"/><ref name="POWO"/>

===Range===
Within Africa, it is found in [[Macaronesia]], (within the [[Madeira Islands]], [[Canary Islands|Canarias]]<ref name="kew"/><ref name="POWO"/>), [[Algeria]], [[Morocco]] and [[Tunisia]].<ref name=Grin/>
It is found in the Asian countries of [[Cyprus]], [[Israel]], [[Lebanon]], [[Syria]] and western [[Turkey]].<ref name=Grin/>
Within Europe,<ref name="Biking"/><ref name="rare"/> it is found in south west [[England]], [[Greece]] (including [[Crete]]), [[Italy]] (including the isles of [[Sardinia]] and [[Sicily]]), [[France]] (including the island of [[Corsica]]), [[Spain]] (including the [[Balearic Islands]]) and [[Portugal]].<ref name=Grin/>

It has [[naturalized]] in the [[Azores]].<ref name=Grin/>

===Habitat===
It is found growing on free draining sandy soils that make up coastal cliffs slopes,<ref name=Jarvis/> and coastal grasslands.<ref name="southwest"/><ref>Nick C. Davidson and Nature Conservancy Council {{google books|8RASAAAAYAAJ|Nature conservation and estuaries in Great Britain (1991)|page=108}}</ref> It can grow on sandy grounds near the sea,<ref name="Seasonal"/> including on [[golf courses]],<ref name=Green/> such as Dawlish Warren course in [[Devon]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Ecology – Warren Golf Club |url=https://devonlinksgolf.com/ecology/ |access-date=8 June 2021}}</ref> which is classified as a [[Site of Special Scientific Interest]] (SSSI).<ref>Robert Stephen Taylor (Editor) {{google books|DWaadZefPHIC|A Practical Guide to Ecological Management of the Golf Course (1995)|page=13}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
[[File:Romulea columnae Mallorca.jpg|thumb|''Romulea columnae'' on [[Mallorca]]]]
In temperate gardens, it is best to grow the plant inside a temperature controlled [[Alpine house]]. It can be grown in containers filled with well-drained, loam-based compost. The plant is allowed to dry in summer after the flowers have faded and the leaves become yellow.<ref name="rare"/>
